body: ### Contributing guidelines - [x] I have read [CONTRIBUTING.md](https://github.com/nvim-mini/mini.nvim/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md) - [x] I have read [CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md](https://github.com/nvim-mini/mini.nvim/blob/main/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md) - [x] I have updated 'mini.nvim' to latest version of the `main` branch ### Module(s) mini.completion ### Neovim version 0.12 (!at least latest Nightly build!) ### Description I have updated to the latest [kotlin-lsp](https://github.com/Kotlin/kotlin-lsp/releases/tag/kotlin-lsp%2Fv261.13587.0) and they re-worked how completions work. I'm not totally sure what they did internally, but it seems to have broken completions. I am filing this issue with mini.completion because I was able to get these completions to work with other plugins such as blink.cmp, but honestly I'm not sure if this is a Mini issue or a general nvim completion issue. Apologies if this issue is in the wrong spot, but just wanted to get the discussion started ### Reproduction ```lua -- Clone latest 'mini.nvim' (requires Git CLI installed) vim.cmd('echo "Installing `mini.nvim`" | redraw') local mini_path = vim.fn.stdpath("data") .. "/site/pack/deps/start/mini.nvim" local clone_cmd = { "git", "clone", "--depth=1", "https://github.com/nvim-mini/mini.nvim", mini_path } vim.fn.system(clone_cmd) vim.cmd('echo "`mini.nvim` is installed" | redraw') -- Make sure 'mini.nvim' is available vim.cmd("packadd mini.nvim") require("mini.deps").setup() -- Add extra setup steps needed to reproduce the behavior require("mini.completion").setup({ lsp_completion = { source_func = "omnifunc", auto_setup = false, process_items = function(items, base) return MiniCompletion.default_process_items(items, base, { kind_priority = { Text = -1, Snippet = 99 } }) end, }, }) vim.api.nvim_create_autocmd("LspAttach", { group = vim.api.nvim_create_augroup("mini-complete-lsp", {}), callback = function(ev) vim.bo[ev.buf].omnifunc = "v:lua.MiniCompletion.completefunc_lsp" end, desc = "Set 'omnifunc'", }) vim.lsp.config("*", { capabilities = MiniCompletion.get_lsp_capabilities() }) vim.lsp.config("kotlin_ls", { filetypes = { "kotlin" }, cmd = { "kotlin-lsp", "--stdio" }, root_markers = { "settings.gradle", -- Gradle (multi-project) "settings.gradle.kts", -- Gradle (multi-project) "pom.xml", -- Maven "build.gradle", -- Gradle "build.gradle.kts", -- Gradle "workspace.json", -- Used to integrate your own build system }, }) vim.lsp.enable("kotlin_ls") ``` When I hit `` to accept this suggestion, it doesn't fill in any text or insert the auto-import. In blink, this all works. (again, I know blink does a lot more, but I just wanted to know if this was something mini.completion can / should support)

comment_data.body:
Thanks for the issue!

> When I hit `<C-y>` to accept this suggestion, it doesn't fill in any text or insert the auto-import. In blink, this all works. (again, I know blink does a lot more, but I just wanted to know if this was something mini.completion can / should support)

Could you please provide more detailed steps to reproduce this? As for somebody who knows nothing about Kotlin. Like what file/project to create, their content, where to put cursor and which keys to press.
Sure, let me find a simple enough open source kotlin project that will work out of the box with this repro

Never mind, I managed to reproduce it with the following setup:

- Add 'mason-org/mason.nvim' installation and setup to 'init.lua' and install `kotlin-lsp` with it. Version `kotlin-lsp/v261.13587.0`.
- Create separate directory (like 'tmp-kotlin') with the following 'hello.kt' file inside of it:

    ```kotlin
    fun main() {
        println("Hello, World!")
    }
    ```
- Start `NVIM_APPNAME=nvim-repro nvim` inside that directory and wait for `kotlin-lsp` to fully load.
- On the line after `println` type `ma`. It should show `main` candidate.
- Select it with `<C-n>` (it shows no info). Accepting it with `<C-y>` has no effect.

Ok thank you so much for this! Kotlin-LSP is really closed source (only jetbrains employees are allowed to contribute), so i'll track that issue but for now I'll try to get it working right with this config change you have provided, appreciate the investigation!

> ... but for now I'll try to get it working right with this config change you have provided, appreciate the investigation!

Good luck! I'll try to see what can be done here, but it looks like a chicken-and-egg problem:
- To know the proper start column you need a processed LSP candidates.
- To process LSP candidates you need to know `base` against which to process. Which is computed based on the start column.

Okay, I did think more about this and had an idea of trying to explicitly opt out from using `insertReplaceEdit` altogether. This should be done by disabling its capability like so:

```lua
local capabilities = MiniCompletion.get_lsp_capabilities()
capabilities.textDocument.completion.completionItem.insertReplaceSupport = false
vim.lsp.config('*', { capabilities = capabilities })
```

But the `kotlin-lsp` doesn't seem to respect this either. I can see during repro that capability is disabled but the server still returns "empty `textEdit` as `insertReplaceEdit`". I don't think tweaking 'mini.completion' specifically to fit this kind of server is a good path forward. Sorry that this happens :(

So I am going to close this as "working as expected".

---

I'll spend some time thinking about whether it is worth adding something like `config.lsp_completion.preprocess_items`. Its main purpose would be to tweak LSP completion output on a server-by-server basis.

It should be enough to provide a valid entry point to solve this issue and possibly some other cases when LSP server behaves not as 'mini.completion' expects (like in #2117).
